title: Seraphim in the snow
hookLine: Seraphim of Sarov shows his friend Motovilov the Spirit's light shining in a snowy forest

lines: TWO MEN IN A SNOWY CLEARING.
cards: Winter in a Russian forest. Snow falls thickly in a clearing. An old monk in a worn white robe, bent with age and old injuries, sits on a tree stump.

Crouched in front of him is a younger man, a landowner, with a question he can't let go of. All his life he's heard that the point of being a Christian is to receive the Holy Spirit. But how would anyone actually know?
What does it look like? The old monk takes him firmly by the shoulders, and something happens in the snow that the younger man later tries to put into words. Today: Seraphim in the snow.

teach.h: THE AIM: ACQUIRE THE HOLY SPIRIT.
teach.b: The monk is Seraphim of Sarov, honored as a saint in the Orthodox Church. The younger man is Nicholas Motovilov, and he wrote the conversation down. Here's how he tells it, paraphrased.
Seraphim says the true aim of the Christian life is the acquiring of the Holy Spirit. Prayer, fasting and good works matter, but as means to that. Motovilov keeps asking how he can know.
So Seraphim grips his shoulders and says, in effect: we are both in the Spirit now. Why won't you look at me? Motovilov says he can't.

teach.h: A FACE BRIGHTER THAN THE SUN.
teach.b: Seraphim's face has become brighter than the sun. Don't be afraid, Seraphim answers. You've become just as bright yourself, or you couldn't see me like this.
Then he asks, again and again, what do you feel?
A quiet, Motovilov answers, a peace he has no words for. A sweetness. Joy.
And warmth, though the snow is still falling and settling on their coats.
Seraphim connects it to Paul, in the King James Bible: "For the kingdom of God is not meat and drink; but righteousness, and peace, and joy in the Holy Ghost."
In Motovilov's telling, peace and joy were not a reward for later. They were the Spirit, there, in the cold.
A saying handed down in Seraphim's name gives today's line its fuller shape: acquire the spirit of peace, and thousands around you will be saved.
In that saying, the change starts small, inside one person, and moves outward like warmth in a cold room.

how: Orthodox Christians honor Seraphim of Sarov as a saint, read Motovilov's account of their conversation, and speak of the aim of the Christian life as acquiring the Holy Spirit.

o: the man who asked Seraphim how to know the Holy Spirit
a Russian bishop who led the church in Moscow
a Russian monk who wrote a book of prayers for winter

p: an old monk, honored as a saint
the friend who wrote it down
the aim of the Christian life

s: Seraphim said prayer and fasting were the goal
he called them means; the aim was acquiring the Holy Spirit.
Motovilov said he felt warm while snow was falling
along with peace, sweetness and joy.
Seraphim wrote the conversation down himself
Motovilov, the younger friend, wrote it down.

games.q: you're Motovilov. the old monk's face has become brighter than the sun, and you can't look at it. what does Seraphim say?
o: close your eyes; this is not for you.
don't be afraid; you're shining too, or you couldn't see me.
games.why: Seraphim told him not to be afraid: he had become just as bright, or he couldn't have seen it. then he kept asking, what do you feel?

practice: If you can, open a window or step outside, and feel the cold air on your face and hands. Breathe, and let Seraphim's question land on you: what do you feel, right now?
Name it honestly, and if you pray, ask quietly for the Spirit's peace; if you don't, let the stillness be enough.

wordCard.voice: Motovilov. The landowner who asked Seraphim of Sarov how to know the Holy Spirit, and said he felt peace, warmth and joy in the falling snow.

orig.note: Greek: peace — the word in Romans 14:17, righteousness, and peace, and joy in the Holy Ghost.

carryVoice: Your line: acquire the spirit of peace. Peace carried into a tense room can change it. Peace to you, until tomorrow.
